newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken says adapts strategy to markets.
newsitem.headline: Heineken says adapts strategy to markets.

text.p: Dutch brewer Heineken NV is adapting its strategy to the different stages of development of the markets in which it operates, chairman Karel Vuursteen said on Monday.

"Next to the loss-making markets or markets that are not yet profitable, profitable markets exist. One can improve one's position on these profitable markets by buying market share," he told reporters.
"Another possibility is to accelerate the development of a particular market," he added, citing Italy, where the company has made several acquisitions.
He said Heineken had about 38 percent of the Italian beer market, which was more stable now.
Vuursteen also mentioned France, where the brewer has made two acquisitions, Fischer Group and Group Saint-Arnould, making it the second biggest brewer after Kronenbourg.

He said Heineken generally chose between setting up brewing operations in a country to produce a "local" brand, and exporting one of its brands, such as the flagship Heineken beer, into a country for a particular segment of the market.
The United States, Hong Kong, Taiwan and China were examples of the "proven (export) concept".
Vuursteen said Europe, North America and Australia were examples of mature and stable markets, while South East Asia and China were emerging markets.
Within Europe, he described Spain as a "battlefield" market, because it was not well structured.
He also said Germany, which suffers from overcapacity, was a disaster.
"The profitability is the world's lowest and it will take years to become lucrative over there," he said.
